title: Surjective closed immersions: module equivalence and finite local models
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $h:T\hookrightarrow Y$ a surjective closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Work on either the small étale or the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with compatible universes and ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaves $A_Y,A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Inverse image $h^*=h^{-1}$ uses the canonical identification $h^{-1}A_Y\cong A_T$, and $h_*$ has its induced $A_Y$-action [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The actual adjunction unit and counit are natural isomorphisms
$$H\xrightarrow{\sim}h_*h^*H,\qquad h^*h_*N\xrightarrow{\sim}N$$
for every module sheaf $H$ on $Y$ and $N$ on $T$. Thus $h^*$ and $h_*$ are quasi-inverse equivalences of module-sheaf categories. For every $A$-module $M$, $h^*\underline M_Y\cong\underline M_T$. A module sheaf $H$ on $Y$ is finite locally constant if and only if $h^*H$ is: here this means that on a covering family of the indicated site it is isomorphic to constant module sheaves with finite $A$-module models [def-constructible-locally-constant, def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. The same equivalence holds with the additional requirement that every local model be a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module. No Noetherianity or uniform nilpotence bound is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09AB (lemma-thickening); lifting to constant-ring module objects and reflection of finite local models. Étale counterpart: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04DZ (theorem-topological-invariance). The module and finite-model clauses are extracted obligations, not literal assertions of the set-topos theorem.

proof.text: Apply the surjective-closed-immersion lemma to $h$: it is a universal homeomorphism, and every base change $h_V:T\times_YV\to V$ is again a surjective closed immersion. The étale invariance theorem gives inverse and direct image equivalences on set sheaves; the pro-étale invariance lemma gives the same conclusion, explicitly for the specified unit and counit. For the étale adjunction these are also the specified unit and counit: a left adjoint to an equivalence is its quasi-inverse, and the adjunction triangles identify its unit and counit with isomorphisms. Thus on either site the actual set-sheaf adjunction of $h$, and of every $h_V$, has invertible unit and counit. None of the cited statements assumes a uniform nilpotence bound or Noetherianity.

Use the constant-coefficient inverse-image theorem with $\Lambda=A$. It identifies module inverse image with abelian inverse image and identifies their units. The finite-product adjunction-lifting theorem identifies the abelian unit with the set-sheaf unit. The coefficient identifications are the canonical ones: the étale module inverse-image proposition gives this explicitly, and the pro-étale constant-ring-map proposition identifies its map with $c_A^h$. The ringed-topos module adjunction gives the stipulated direct-image action. Hence the actual module unit $H\to h_*h^*H$ has an invertible underlying sheaf by step 1. A linear map with an invertible underlying sheaf has linear inverse: from $f(ax)=af(x)$ apply $f^{-1}$, and similarly for addition. Thus every module unit is invertible. The same reasoning applies to all $h_V$.

The module direct image reflects isomorphisms: its underlying set functor is the equivalence in step 1, and an underlying inverse to a linear map is linear by step 2. For $N$ on $T$, the adjunction triangle says $h_*\varepsilon_N\circ\eta_{h_*N}=1$. Since $\eta_{h_*N}$ is invertible, $h_*\varepsilon_N$ is invertible. Reflection gives that the actual counit $\varepsilon_N:h^*h_*N\to N$ is invertible. The unit and counit are natural by their adjunction, so the stipulated functors, with these actual maps, are quasi-inverse equivalences. In particular $h^*$ is fully faithful, as is each $h_V^*$.

source.place: Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), adjunction triangles and elementary inversion of linear maps

proof.text: Apply the geometric inverse-image constant-module lemma with $R=A$ to the induced geometric morphism for any scheme morphism $f:U\to V$ on either indicated site. The canonical coefficient identification and actual module inverse image agree with those used here by step 2 (applied to $f$). The cited statement supplies the canonical $A_U$-linear isomorphism $f^*\underline M_V\cong\underline M_U$, natural in every $A$-linear map of models, for arbitrary $A$-modules $M$. In particular this proves the required comparison for $h$ and all morphisms between site objects and base changes used in steps 5–7; no finiteness of $M$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi), as in the cited existing geometric constant-module comparison lemma

proof.text: The étale localization lemma identifies $Y_{\mathrm{Et}}/V$ with $V_{\mathrm{Et}}$ for an étale object $V\to Y$. In the inverse-image colimit formula at $W\to V$, the pair $(W\to Y,\mathrm{graph}:W\to V\times_YW)$ is initial in the indexing category, since any other pair is exactly a map $W\to U$ over $Y$ with that graph compatibility. Its opposite is final, so the colimit is $H(W)$; sheafification leaves this restriction sheaf unchanged. Thus inverse image along the site object is localized restriction, including the module action by the constant-coefficient theorem. The pro-étale object-restriction theorem gives the corresponding identification there. The constant-coefficient theorem also supplies compatibility with composition and localized restrictions. If $\{V_i\to Y\}$ trivializes $H$ with models $M_i$, then $\{T\times_YV_i\to T\}$ trivializes $h^*H$ with the identical models by this compatibility and step 4. This is a cover étale-locally by covering-preserving étale base change; pro-étale-locally, weakly étale base change and fpqc covering base change verify the two covering conditions. The locality definitions allow the models to vary with the cover members.

source.place: lemma-pullback-locally-constant; sites.tex Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi), localized inverse images

proof.text: For reflection on the étale site, choose a cover $\{U_i\to T\}$ and module trivializations $(h^*H)|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}_{U_i}$. Essential surjectivity of étale base change supplies $V_i\to Y$ étale with $T\times_YV_i\cong U_i$. The covering-reflection lemma says that $\{V_i\to Y\}$ is a cover, because its base change is the chosen cover. Write $h_i:U_i\to V_i$ for the base-changed $h$. By step 1 it is a surjective closed immersion. Compatibility with localized restrictions identifies $h_i^*(H|_{V_i})$ with $(h^*H)|_{U_i}$, and step 4 identifies $h_i^*\underline{M_i}_{V_i}$ with $\underline{M_i}_{U_i}$. Thus the chosen trivialization is an isomorphism between the images of $H|_{V_i}$ and $\underline{M_i}_{V_i}$. By full faithfulness in step 3, lift it and its inverse uniquely; faithfulness makes both composites identities. This yields an $A_{V_i}$-linear trivialization with the same model $M_i$.

source.place: Tag 04DZ (theorem-topological-invariance), Tag 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance); lifting module trivializations by full faithfulness

proof.text: For reflection on the pro-étale site, let $C=\{U_a\to T\}$ trivialize $h^*H$ with models $M_a$. Apply the surjective-closed-cover-refinement theorem: it supplies a cover $B=\{V_b\to Y\}$ and, for each $b$, an index $a$ and a cartesian square $W_b=T\times_YV_b$, with maps $q_b:W_b\to V_b$, $p_b:W_b\to T$, and $r_b:W_b\to U_a$ over $T$. Here $q_b$ is the base change of $h$, so step 1 applies to it. Both $W_b\to T$ and $U_a\to T$ are site objects, and the between-objects lemma makes $r_b$ weakly étale. Inverse image along a pro-étale site object is localized restriction by the object-restriction theorem. Pull back the chosen trivialization along $r_b$. Compatibility with composition and restriction identifies its left side with $q_b^*(H|_{V_b})$, because the two composites $W_b\to Y$ agree in the square; step 4 identifies its right side with $\underline{M_a}_{W_b}$. Also $q_b^*\underline{M_a}_{V_b}\cong\underline{M_a}_{W_b}$. Lift this isomorphism and its inverse through the fully faithful $q_b^*$ of step 3. As in step 6 the lifted composites are identities, yielding $H|_{V_b}\cong\underline{M_a}_{V_b}$. Since $B$ is a cover this is the required pro-étale trivializing datum. It requires only refinement of $C$, not lifting every weakly étale object of $T$ to $Y$.

source.place: Tags 09AB (lemma-thickening), 09BK (lemma-closed-immersion-affines); covering refinement as stated in the cited existing node; localized module restrictions

proof.text: In steps 5–7 the scalar model is always the very same $A$-module as before pullback or descent, merely reindexed by a refined cover. Thus if the models are finite, they remain finite, and if each is a direct summand of some $A^n$, the same splitting maps and the same $n$ certify that property after either direction. This proves both local-model equivalences. The empty schemes cause no exception: a surjective closed immersion has empty source exactly when its target is empty; an empty covering is allowed and the local conditions are vacuous. The zero ring and zero module are also included throughout; no cancellation, nonzero element, or positive rank was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q80-4227bccb2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full: all 8 steps and the statements of all 21 cited nodes. I read the unit sk-lem-sf-flat-model and how the parent det-sf-flat-model-generation uses the item in clause (2). Sources read: Stacks 09AB (proetale.tex l.4962) and 04DZ (etale-cohomology.tex l.6354). The statement is unchanged and true: a surjective closed immersion is integral, universally injective and surjective. I tested it on id, Spec k→Spec k[ε], a nil but not nilpotent ideal, the empty scheme, the zero ring and the zero module. Step checks: (1) universal homeomorphism and base change, with étale and pro-étale invariance for the actual unit and counit. (2) The module unit equals the abelian unit (lem-pe), which equals the set unit (adjunction-lifting lemma); the coefficient maps are canonical. (3) The counit follows from the triangle identity and reflection of isomorphisms. (4) lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module states exactly the constant-module comparison used. (5) The graph pair is initial, so the colimit is H(W); pro-étale restriction uses the object-restriction lemma; covers are preserved by base change (fpqc for pro-étale). (6) and (7) Reflection works by lifting covers, or by the Lean cover-refinement node with r_b weakly étale, plus full faithfulness of the base-changed pullback. (8) The models are literally unchanged. The declared tool_uses are acceptable; the other off-unit citations are Mathlib leaves or closed in slopmaster2. No cycle, no new nodes, no duplicate: lemma-constructible-universal-homeomorphism-invariance and the condensed nodes are narrower or about different coefficients. Batch-5 check on lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance: it is Stacks 09AB, a general pro-étale topological-invariance result. Neither the trace formula nor Poincaré duality gives it. Its full closure (1146 nodes) contains no other sec-trace-formula or sec-poincare-duality node, no batch-4 target and no nt-assume leaf. The item's pro-étale clauses genuinely need it, so I accept the citation as outside the assumed statements. No fixes.
